track.why: 3 Sep 2020 logged NW Couloir; report describes the Peggy Pond approach, the cairned shoulder, the two spires at the base, chockstone and tunnel, matching our text; round trip from the trailhead (30 m start, 23 m end), summit 10 m. Caveat: the track also visits Mount Daniel (its highest point), so the owner may want to trim it.

otherTracksConsidered.why: Aug 2021 NW Couloir, round trip, but no report and it also includes Mount Daniel.
Sep 2021 NW Couloir report, but no track points.

facts.text: In September a cairned line crosses heather benches up the west shoulder to the couloir base; the steep loose talus alternative is slower.
Going counter-clockwise round Peggy Pond reaches the rock field by a path; traversing high and clockwise through steep heather is much worse.
The tunnel under the chockstone is a tight squeeze; push the pack ahead of you.
A helmet is essential; a short handline covers the steps, and September parties carried a rope but did not use it.
September: low in the streambed approach a 10-15 ft class 4 rock step splits the gully; the right side is easier.

track.why: 3 Aug 2025 report: gully approach, short rope pitch to a boulder festooned with slings, traverse to the summit block, rappel back down the gully, matching our SW face/horn-rappel text; track starts/ends 23-32 m from the trailhead pin and peaks 9 m from our summit. The report does not use the route name, so identity rests on the description.

otherTracksConsidered.why: Logged Southwest gully (30 Sep 2012) but one-way, ending at Nosh Nosh Wahtum 972 m from the trailhead.
Same day and party as 2929501, no report.
8 Jun 2024 snow ascent, no report, line unknown.

facts.text: Where the faint path below the base ends, an exposed notch scramble on the right reaches a flat bench; then head left toward the tall spire marking the approach gully, staying left of the gully floor on an exposed ledge to avoid rockfall.
The alternate descent gully on the skier-right side is full of loose rock with narrow choke points; move one at a time.
In early August the party roped for the pitch above the gully and the traverse to the summit block, and unroped at the block.

notes: NE Buttress, NE Ridge and SE Chimney have no identifiable track. Harvested start clusters all sit within 25 m of the trailhead pin, so no pin work needed.
